claim.pdf_says: 14.9.28.4   General rules  (a fourth-level clause, printed in the same style and at the same level as 14.9.28.1 General, 14.9.28.2 General formats and 14.9.28.3 Syntax rules, all subordinate to 14.9.28 PERFORM statement)
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.28.4 General rules  (H2 - the same level the markdown gives the parent clause '## 14.9.28 PERFORM statement', while its siblings are '### 14.9.28.1 General' and '### 14.9.28.2 General formats')
claim.why_it_matters: The clause is promoted out of its parent: in any generated TOC or outline view 14.9.28.4 no longer nests under 14.9.28 PERFORM statement, and the sibling clauses of the same statement sit at two different depths. The dominant convention in this document is '###' for x.y.z.w clauses (162 occurrences versus 40 at '##').

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) Nothing is missing. The kind 'missing-heading' is factually wrong. The PDF (E:/Temp/specrecon/v714/spec_p714.png, printed page 684) shows the bold heading '14.9.28.4 General rules' immediately after syntax rule 16) and before 'ALL FORMATS' / general rule 1). specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29215 carries '## 14.9.28.4 General rules', preceded by the anchor ''. Clause number, title, position and surrounding content all match the PDF exactly. Zero text, zero normative content, zero choice indicator is lost or altered. (2) The claim's core premise -- that markdown heading depth encodes clause nesting in this document -- is false, and I verified it directly. The ancestors of this clause are: ## 14 Procedure division (line 23252) ## 14.9 Statements (line 25225) ## 14.9.28 PERFORM statement (line 29049) ## 14.9.28.4 General rules (line 29215) All four sit at '##'. Clause 14 -- three levels further up than the parent the claim says 14.9.28.4 was 'promoted out of' -- is itself at '##'. There is no depth-encoding convention here for 14.9.28.4 to violate; '##' is what the transcription gives clause 14 and clause 14.9 as well. Hierarchy in this transcription is carried entirely by the dotted clause number and the '' anchor, both of which are transcribed correctly. (3) The claim's supporting statistic is wrong by roughly 4x. Measured over specs/ISO_COBOL.md: 620 four-level (x.y.z.w) headings at '###' and 162 at '##' -- not the claimed '162 occurrences versus 40 at ##'. The claim appears to have cited the '##' count as the '###' count. (4) It is not a page-714 finding and not a one-off promotion. The '##' four-level headings are a systematic transcription pattern dominated by exactly two titles: 37 'General rules' and 23 'Syntax rules'. Every neighbouring statement clause shows it -- '## 14.9.26.4 General rules', '## 14.9.27.4 General rules', '## 14.9.2.4', '## 14.9.10.4', '## 14.9.30.4', etc. Within PERFORM itself the claim's own sibling list is selectively incomplete: it names 14.9.28.1 and 14.9.28.2 as '###' siblings but omits that '## 14.9.28.3 Syntax rules' (line 29153) is ALSO at '##'. So 14.9.28.4 was not singled out; .3 and .4 share one level and .1 and .2 share another, which is a generator artifact affecting 162 headings document-wide, not a page-714 defect. Markdown '#' depth is markup introduced by the transcription pipeline; the PDF has no such construct. This is a formatting-only difference that changes no meaning -- an explicit rejection ground.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading '14.9.28.4 General rules' is present in the markdown with its number, title, anchor and position matching the PDF exactly; nothing is missing. The only difference is the markdown '#' nesting depth, which is transcription markup with no counterpart in the PDF and which does not encode clause hierarchy anywhere in this document -- '## 14 Procedure division', '## 14.9 Statements' and '## 14.9.28 PERFORM statement' are all likewise at '##'. If the '##'/'###' split for four-level clauses is ever worth normalizing, it is a single document-wide cosmetic pass over 162 headings (dominated by 37 'General rules' and 23 'Syntax rules' titles), not a per-page spec-reconciliation finding. The claim's cited counts ('162 versus 40') are also wrong; the true figures are 620 at '###' and 162 at '##'.
